mainTopic: Witnesses for קידוש החודש: relatives, disqualified witnesses, breaking שבת to testify, and vouching for unknown witnesses
overview: This amud finishes the first פרק of ראש השנה and begins the second. First, a ברייתא records רבי יהודה's claim that it was זפר, the head of גדר, and not רבי עקיבא, who held back the witnesses of the new moon. Next, a משנה brings a מחלוקת: the תנא קמא says a father and son cannot count as a pair of witnesses, while רבי שמעון says relatives are fit for עדות החודש. רבי לוי finds רבי שמעון's source in "החדש הזה לכם", and the רבנן read that פסוק differently. After a back-and-forth between רב הונא and רב חנן בר רבא, שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. Another משנה lists people unfit to testify, and רב אשי learns from it that a גזלן דדבריהם may testify to free a woman to remarry. The last משנה of the פרק allows witnesses to break שבת to reach בית דין, based on "במועדם". After the הדרן, the new פרק opens: an unknown witness must bring someone to vouch for him, because of the בייתוסים. The גמרא starts to ask what "another" means, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the story of the forty pairs of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the previous משנה: more than forty pairs of witnesses were traveling, and רבי עקיבא held them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: there was a story where more than forty pairs of witnesses passed through, and רבי עקיבא held them back, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up a discussion of it. This is a setup line, and the next step will comment on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, witnesses were traveling to ירושלים on שבת to testify about the new moon. רבי עקיבא stopped them, thinking that so many witnesses did not need to break שבת. The גמרא brings up this story because a ברייתא tells it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident that actually happened
A pair (here, a pair of witnesses)
He held them back / detained them
Short for וְכוּלֵּיהּ, meaning 'etc.' (the quote continues)

phrases.english: There was an incident where more than forty pairs passed through
phrases.notes: Pairs of witnesses on their way to testify about the new moon

phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva detained them, etc.
phrases.notes: He stopped them in לוד so they would not break שבת

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening quote of the משנה (continuing from the previous daf)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה reports that רבי עקיבא held back many witnesses from traveling on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says it was זפר, not רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה, who says רבי עקיבא would never have held back the witnesses. It was זפר, the head of גדר, and רבן גמליאל removed him from his position.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה said, 'Heaven forbid that רבי עקיבא held them back! Rather, זפר, the head of גדר, held them back. רבן גמליאל sent word, and they removed him from his high position.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה disagrees with the משנה about who stopped the witnesses. He says it was a local leader named זפר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that stopping the witnesses was a real mistake. A גדול like רבי עקיבא would not have made it. The proof that it was a mistake is that רבן גמליאל punished the man who did it by removing him from office.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was taught' — introduces a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה)
Heaven forbid
The head (leader) of the town גדר
They removed him from his high position

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying the story never happened. He agrees someone stopped the witnesses. He only disagrees about who did it.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Heaven forbid that Rabbi Akiva detained them!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שַׁזְפַּר רֹאשָׁהּ שֶׁל גֶּדֶר עִיכְּבָן,
phrases.english: Rather, Zefer, the head of Geder, detained them,
and Rabban Gamliel sent word
and they removed him from his high office.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עִיכְּבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the story quoted in Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stopping the witnesses was wrong. It was done by זפר, not רבי עקיבא, and זפר was removed from office for it.
steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses for the new moon should not be stopped, even on שבת. The man who stopped them was punished, which shows how important their testimony was.

steps.title: A father and son should both go, but not as a pair
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a father and son who saw the new moon should both go to בית דין. They cannot count together as two witnesses. But if one of them is disqualified, the other can pair up with a different witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A father and son who saw the new moon should go. This is not because they can join together as witnesses. It is because if one of them is disqualified, the second can join together with someone else.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a ruling about relatives who saw the new moon. It explains why both should go even though they cannot testify as a pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally relatives (קרובים) are not allowed to testify together. Even so, both should travel. If one of them turns out to be unfit, for example because a problem is found in his testimony, the other is still available to pair with an outside witness.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין — 'our משנה'
A father and his son
They join together (count as a pair of witnesses)
He will be disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying the father and son testify together. They each go separately as a backup, so each one can pair with a non-relative.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אָב וּבְנוֹ שֶׁרָאוּ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ — יֵלְכוּ.
phrases.english: MISHNA: A father and his son who saw the new moon should go.
Not that they join together with each other,
but rather so that if one of them is disqualified,
the second may join together with another witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָב וּבְנוֹ שֶׁרָאוּ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ — יֵלְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: relatives as witnesses for the new moon
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relatives cannot count together as a pair for testimony about the new moon, but each may serve as a backup witness.

steps.title: רבי שמעון allows relatives to testify about the month
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees with the תנא קמא. He says a father, a son, and all relatives are fit to testify together about the new moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: A father and his son, and all relatives, are fit for testimony about the new month.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the opposing opinion. He says the usual rule against relatives testifying does not apply to testimony about the new moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא in Step 3 treats עדות החודש like any other testimony, where relatives are disqualified. רבי שמעון makes עדות החודש an exception, so a father and son could serve as the two witnesses. The category is still testimony; רבי שמעון only removes the rule against relatives in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives
Fit / valid (allowed to testify)
Testimony about seeing the new moon

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the גמרא will look for the source of רבי שמעון's exception. That search is the topic of Step 6.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
A father and his son and all relatives
are fit for testimony about the new month.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אָב וּבְנוֹ וְכׇל הַקְּרוֹבִין כְּשֵׁרִין לְעֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא in Step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relatives may testify together about the new moon.

steps.title: The story of טוביה הרופא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells of טוביה הרופא, who saw the new moon with his son and his freed slave. The כהנים accepted him and his son but rejected the slave. The בית דין accepted him and the slave but rejected the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: There was a story with טוביה the doctor. He saw the new moon in ירושלים together with his son and his freed slave. The כהנים accepted him and his son and rejected his slave. When they came before the בית דין, the judges accepted him and his slave and rejected his son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי brings a real-life story about relatives testifying. In it, the official בית דין did not accept a father and son as a pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים rejected the freed slave because they held that only witnesses of Jewish birth were acceptable, and they accepted father and son together. The בית דין did the reverse: a freed slave is a full Jew and may testify, but a son cannot pair with his father. This supports the תנא קמא against רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The doctor
A freed slave (who becomes a full Jew)
The priests
The rabbinical court

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two groups. The כהנים rejected the slave. The בית דין, the official authority, rejected the son. Even so, the גמרא later rules like רבי שמעון (see Steps 9 and 15).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּטוֹבִיָּה הָרוֹפֵא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: There was an incident with Toviyya the doctor
who saw the new moon in Jerusalem,
he and his son and his freed slave,
and the priests accepted him and his son
and disqualified his slave.
And when they came before the court,
they accepted him and his slave,
and disqualified his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּטוֹבִיָּה הָרוֹפֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real incident that supports the תנא קמא (Step 3) against רבי שמעון (Step 4)
steps.raayaObject: The view of the תנא קמא that relatives cannot testify together about the new moon
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of the בית דין in the case of טוביה הרופא, which rejected his son but accepted his freed slave
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the בית דין rejected a son testifying alongside his father, and it accepted a freed slave as a valid witness.

steps.title: רבי לוי gives רבי שמעון's source from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי explains that רבי שמעון learns his view from the פסוק "החדש הזה לכם". The month was given to משה and אהרן, who were brothers, so testimony about the month is valid even from relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי לוי said: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The Torah says, 'And ה׳ said to משה and אהרן in the land of מצרים, saying: This month shall be for you.' This means: this testimony shall be valid through you, even though you are brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבי לוי, who asks where רבי שמעון gets his view and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks to משה and אהרן together and says "לכם" — 'for you' — about the new month. משה and אהרן were brothers, who normally cannot testify together. רבי לוי reads the פסוק as saying that for the month, even relatives like them are valid witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא — the discussion of the משנה
What is the reason?
As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
'This month shall be for you' (שמות יב:ב)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives רבי שמעון's exception a basis in the Torah. The rule comes from the פסוק itself, not from a general idea that new-moon testimony is less serious.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Levi said:
What is the reason for Rabbi Shimon's opinion?

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן
phrases.english: As it is written: "And the Lord said to Moses and to Aaron
in the land of Egypt, saying:
This month shall be for you" —
this testimony shall be valid through you.
phrases.notes: Even through two brothers like משה and אהרן

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא returns to רבי שמעון's view (Step 4) and gives its source
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From "החדש הזה לכם", said to the brothers משה and אהרן, we learn that relatives may testify about the new moon.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן explain the פסוק 'החדש הזה לכם', since they do not learn from it that relatives may testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? (How do they explain this פסוק?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: if the רבנן do not use 'החדש הזה לכם' to allow relatives, what do they learn from it? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי just showed that רבי שמעון learns his view from the word 'לכם', meaning משה and אהרן, who were brothers. The רבנן disagree with רבי שמעון's ruling, so they must read the פסוק in another way. The גמרא wants to know what that reading is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (the majority view, here the תנא קמא)
'And the Rabbis?', a short formula asking how the other side handles a source

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? (How do they explain the verse?)
phrases.notes: A one-word question formula. It is short because the full question is understood from context.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up רבי לוי's source for רבי שמעון by asking how the opposing side reads the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן interpret 'החדש הזה לכם' if not as allowing relatives to testify.

steps.title: The verse means the leaders control the calendar
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read 'לכם' to mean that this testimony is handed over to great leaders like משה and אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This testimony shall be handed over to you (to people like you).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן read 'לכם' differently. To them it means that setting the month is given over to great leaders like משה and אהרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the emphasis is on WHO controls the calendar: the top leaders of each generation. It has nothing to do with whether relatives may testify. This way they keep the פסוק meaningful without accepting רבי שמעון's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony
Handed over to you (given into your authority)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same word in a פסוק can support two different readings. That is why the מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and the רבנן can stand.

phrases.english: This testimony shall be given over to you (and those like you).
phrases.notes: 'לכם' is read as referring to the authority of great leaders, not to the family relationship between משה and אהרן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן read 'לכם' as giving authority over the calendar to the outstanding leaders of each generation.

steps.title: רב חנן בר רבא rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יוסי's story in the משנה, and רב חנן בר רבא rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי יוסי said: There was a story with טוביה הרופא…' רב חנן בר רבא said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the start of רבי יוסי's story from the משנה. Then רב חנן בר רבא gives a ruling: the הלכה is like רבי שמעון, so relatives may testify together about the new moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story, the בית דין accepted טוביה but rejected his son, so father and son could not count as a pair. That seems to support the רבנן. Even so, רב חנן rules like רבי שמעון, and this sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה (the final ruling)
In accordance with רבי שמעון
Etc. (the rest of the quote is understood)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: There was an incident with Toviyya the doctor, etc.
Rav Chanan bar Rava said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא הִלְכְתָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where each side gets its view to the practical question of whose view is the הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: relatives may testify together about the new moon.

steps.title: רב הונא objects: רבי יוסי and a real story say otherwise
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks how רב חנן can rule like רבי שמעון when רבי יוסי, backed by an actual מעשה, supports the opposing view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to רב חנן בר רבא: You have רבי יוסי AND a real story, and yet you say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא challenges the ruling. He has two reasons against it: רבי יוסי holds the other way, and there was a real case where בית דין acted the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things work against רבי שמעון here. First, the הלכה usually follows רבי יוסי against his colleagues. Second, a real-life story (מעשה) is strong proof, because it shows what בית דין actually did. In the story, the בית דין rejected the son, which goes against רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident, which counts as strong proof for practical הלכה
And you say…?! (an expression of surprise in a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said to Rav Chanan bar Rava:
Rabbi Yosei and an actual incident (support the other view),
and you say the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנן בר רבא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's authority, together with a real court case that rejected the son, should outweigh רבי שמעון's view.

steps.title: רב חנן: רב never objected to my ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן defends himself: he said this ruling in front of רב many times, and רב never corrected him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But many times I said in front of רב that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, and he never said anything to me!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן answers the challenge with a proof. His great teacher רב heard him say this ruling many times and never objected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנן's argument is that a teacher's silence means agreement. If רב had disagreed, he would have corrected him. So רב must have agreed that the הלכה is like רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Many times
In front of רב
And he did not say anything at all to me

phrases.english: He (Rav Chanan) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא זִמְנִין סַגִּיאִין אֲמַרִית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
phrases.english: But many times I said before Rav
that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon
and he never said anything to me!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא זִמְנִין סַגִּיאִין אֲמַרִית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the ruling against רב הונא's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב heard this ruling many times and stayed silent, which is taken as his agreement.

steps.title: רב הונא asks: How did you learn the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks רב חנן which version of the משנה he learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How did you learn the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks a short question to test רב חנן's proof. This sets up the answer that will undo the proof from רב's silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא suspects that רב חנן learned the משנה in a different version. If so, רב's silence may mean something other than what רב חנן thinks.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you learn (the text of the משנה)?

phrases.english: He said to him: How did you learn (the mishna)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the proof from step 11 by asking about רב חנן's version of the text.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which version of the משנה, with which names on each view, רב חנן had learned.

steps.title: רב חנן learned the names reversed
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן says he learned the משנה with the names switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The opposite way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן admits that he learned the משנה 'אפכא', the reverse way. In his version, the names on the two opinions were switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב חנן's version, the view that our משנה gives to רבי שמעון belonged to someone else. So the name 'רבי שמעון' was attached to a different opinion in his text.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite (with the names reversed)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אפכא' does not mean that רב חנן changed the הלכה. It means the NAMES in his text were switched. So when he said 'like רבי שמעון', he was pointing to a different opinion than the one we call רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: He said to him: The opposite (with the attributions reversed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learned the משנה with the opinions attributed in reverse.

steps.title: That is why רב stayed silent
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that רב was silent only because, in רב חנן's switched version, the ruling came out correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That is why he never said anything to you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא knocks down רב חנן's proof. רב did not correct him because, by רב חנן's reversed text, his ruling matched the correct הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the names were switched, 'like רבי שמעון' in רב חנן's text really meant the view that we attribute to the רבנן and רבי יוסי. So רב's silence actually supports the opposite of what רב חנן claimed. The proof from silence falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of this / that is why

phrases.english: He (Rav Huna) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא אֲמַר לָךְ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: That is why he never said anything to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא אֲמַר לָךְ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 13 to reject the proof of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רב's silence. It does not settle the הלכה by itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב's silence was agreement with the reversed text, so it says nothing in favor of our רבי שמעון.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of transmitters, שמואל is quoted ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: טבי son of מרי טבי said that מר עוקבא said that שמואל said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: Even after רב חנן's proof failed, the גמרא brings another authority, שמואל, who also rules like רבי שמעון. This gives רבי שמעון's view solid support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from רב's silence was rejected, but the ruling itself is now backed by שמואל, passed down through a chain of three people. So רבי שמעון's view stands: relatives may testify together about the new moon.

keyTerms.meaning: A major early אמורא in בבל
An אמורא, the head of the court in בבל, who passes on שמואל's ruling

steps.whatToRemember: The final word in this sugya: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, so relatives may testify together about the new moon. This holds even though רבי יוסי's story seemed to point the other way and רב's silence turned out not to be a proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that knocking down one proof does not knock down a ruling. A new authority can still establish the הלכה.

phrases.english: Tavi, son of Mari Tavi, said
that Mar Ukva said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר טָבִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּמָרִי טָבִי אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from רב was rejected, brings independent support for the same ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: relatives are fit to testify together about the new moon.

steps.title: New משנה: who is unfit to testify
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists people who are unfit to testify and gives a rule comparing them to a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the people who are unfit: one who plays with dice, those who lend with interest, those who race pigeons, those who trade in שביעית produce, and slaves. This is the rule: any testimony that a woman is unfit for, these are also unfit for.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists five types of people who cannot testify, and then gives a general rule: wherever a woman cannot testify, these people cannot either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the people on this list earn money in dishonest or forbidden ways, so they are not trusted as witnesses. Slaves are a separate category. The closing rule ties them all to a woman's status, so they are unfit in the same cases where a woman is unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: People unfit (disqualified) to testify
One who gambles with dice
Those who lend with interest
Pigeon racers (who bet on the races)
Merchants who trade in produce of the Sabbatical Year
This is the general rule

phrases.english: MISHNA:
These are the ones who are unfit (to testify):
one who plays with dice, and those who lend with interest,
and those who race pigeons, and merchants of Sabbatical-Year produce, and slaves.
This is the principle:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֵדוּת שֶׁאֵין הָאִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁירָה לָהּ,
phrases.english: Any testimony for which a woman is not fit,
these too are not fit for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: which kinds of people are disqualified as witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gamblers, lenders with interest, pigeon racers, traders in שביעית produce, and slaves are unfit to testify in every case where a woman is unfit.

steps.title: The reverse side of the משנה's rule about a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's rule in reverse: wherever a woman is fit to testify, these disqualified people are fit too.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that any testimony for which a woman is fit, they too are fit for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a simple inference from the last line of the משנה. It is setting up the next move, where רב אשי applies this inference to a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said: 'any testimony a woman is unfit for, these people are also unfit for.' The גמרא flips it: if they are equal to a woman when she is unfit, they are also equal to her when she is fit. Where we accept a woman's testimony, we also accept theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that analyzes the משנה
'This implies'; introduces an inference from the wording
Fit / valid (to testify)
They too

phrases.english: GEMARA: This implies that [testimony] a woman is fit for,
phrases.notes: The reverse reading (דיוק) of the משנה's 'כל עדות שאין האשה כשירה לה'.

phrases.english: they too are fit for it.
phrases.notes: 'They' = the people the משנה listed as unfit witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the closing rule of the משנה in step 16 in reverse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who are unfit only where a woman is unfit are fit wherever a woman is fit.

steps.title: A rabbinic-level robber may testify to free a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes from the inference that a גזלן דדבריהם is a valid witness for עדות אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This tells us that a robber by rabbinic law is fit to testify for a woman (that her husband died, so she may remarry).
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes the inference from step 17 and states the practical הלכה that follows from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several people in the משנה, like a dice player, are not real thieves. They are called 'robbers' only by rabbinic law (גזלן דדבריהם). The חכמים let a woman testify that a husband died so his wife may remarry. So these rabbinic-level robbers, who equal a woman, may also give that testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This tells us'; draws a practical conclusion from a source
A 'robber' only by rabbinic law, not a true thief by Torah law
Testimony that a woman's husband died, allowing her to remarry

steps.confusionAlert: 'עדות אשה' here does not mean testimony given BY a woman in general. It is the special testimony that frees a woman (an עגונה) to remarry, where the חכמים relaxed the usual rules for witnesses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה: someone disqualified only by rabbinic law can still help free an עגונה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: That is to say,
a robber by rabbinic law
phrases.notes: Like the dice player or the pigeon racer from the משנה.

phrases.english: are fit for testimony regarding a woman [to remarry].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the inference of step 17 to a concrete halachic case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גזלן דדבריהם is a valid witness for עדות אשה.

steps.title: Helping a witness who cannot walk or fears bandits
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a witness of the new moon who cannot walk is carried, even in a bed, and witnesses may carry clubs if bandits threaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who saw the new moon but cannot walk is brought on a donkey, or even in a bed. If bandits lie in wait for them, they take clubs in their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that we make every effort, even on שבת, to bring a witness of the new moon to בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you may not carry someone on a donkey or a bed on שבת, and you may not carry weapons. Here the testimony is needed to set the month, so these things are allowed. The point is that nothing should stop the witness from arriving.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our משנה'; marks the start of a משנה
Saw the new moon
A bed (used here as a stretcher)
Lying in wait for them (bandits)
Clubs / sticks

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who saw the new moon
but is unable to walk —
they bring him on a donkey,
even in a bed.
And if [bandits] lie in wait for them, —
they take clubs in their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on bringing witnesses of the moon to בית דין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness of the new moon who cannot walk may be carried, even in a bed, and witnesses may carry clubs for protection, even on שבת.

steps.title: Food for a long trip and the limit for breaking שבת
steps.stepSummary: For a long trip, witnesses may carry food. They may break שבת for a journey of up to a night and a day, based on the פסוק 'במועדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the trip is long, they take food in their hands. For a journey of a night and a day, people may break שבת and go out to testify about the new moon. As it says: 'These are the festivals of ה' which you shall call in their set times.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues, allowing witnesses to carry food. It then gives the reason and the limit for all these permissions, with a source from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying food on שבת would normally be forbidden. It is allowed here because witnesses may break שבת for a trip of up to a night and a day. The פסוק says the festivals must be declared 'במועדם', at their proper time, so the month must be set on time even if that means breaking שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Food / provisions
A journey of a night and a day (the limit)
They desecrate (break) שבת
In their set time

steps.whatToRemember: Setting the month on time (במועדם) is important enough to override שבת, for a trip of up to a night and a day.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'במועדם' explains all the permissions in this משנה: carrying the witness, the clubs, and the food.

phrases.english: And if it was a long journey —
they take food in their hands.
For a journey of a night and a day,
they may desecrate Shabbat
and go out to testify about the new moon,
as it is stated: 'These are the festivals of the Lord'
'which you shall declare in their set times.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה and gives the reason and source for all its permissions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses may carry food and break שבת for a journey of up to a night and a day to testify about the new moon, because the festivals must be declared במועדם.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter ארבעה ראשי שנים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the first פרק of ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'ארבעה ראשי שנים'.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the first chapter, ארבעה ראשי שנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional closing that expresses our wish to come back and learn this chapter again. No new הלכה is taught here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you'; the chapter-closing formula
'Four New Years'; the name of the first פרק of ראש השנה

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Four New Years'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after its final משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first chapter of ראש השנה, ארבעה ראשי שנים, is complete.

steps.title: An unknown witness brings someone to vouch for him
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens. If the בית דין does not recognize a witness of the new moon, another person is sent along to vouch for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they (the בית דין) do not know him, they (his town) send another person with him to vouch for him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a new משנה. It says that if the judges do not know the witness who saw the new moon, someone else comes with him to confirm that he is a trustworthy person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges must know that a witness is reliable before accepting his testimony about the new moon. When they do not know him, the problem is solved by sending a companion who can vouch for his character. The word "another" is vague, and the גמרא will soon ask exactly what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: They recognize or know (here: the בית דין knows the witness)
They send
Another person
To testify about him, meaning to vouch for him

steps.confusionAlert: The companion is not testifying that he saw the moon. He is only testifying about the first witness, that he is a reliable person.

phrases.english: If they do not recognize him —
phrases.notes: "They" refers to the בית דין in ירושלים.

phrases.english: they send another with him to testify about him.
phrases.notes: The people of his town send someone to vouch for his trustworthiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the new פרק right after the closing formula of the first פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unknown witness of the new moon must be accompanied by someone who vouches for him.

steps.title: The history: from anyone, to only known witnesses
steps.stepSummary: Originally, testimony about the new moon was accepted from anyone. After the בייתוסים corrupted the process, the חכמים enacted that only known witnesses be accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they accepted testimony about the new month from any person. Once the בייתוסים caused damage, they enacted that they would accept testimony only from people who are known.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains where the rule of the previous step comes from. It was a later enactment (תקנה), made because of the בייתוסים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In early times the judges did not check who the witness was. The בייתוסים, a sect that rejected the חכמים, tried to manipulate the calendar with false witnesses. As the גמרא later explains, they did this by hiring false witnesses. So the חכמים made a תקנה that a witness must be known, or must be vouched for, which is the rule in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, in earlier times
Testimony about sighting the new moon
They caused damage or corruption
A sect that rejected the חכמים' tradition
They enacted a rabbinic decree (תקנה)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the requirement for a known witness is a protective תקנה, not the original law. This is a common pattern in which the חכמים tighten a rule after people abuse it.

phrases.english: At first they would accept
testimony of the new month from any person.
phrases.notes: No check of who the witness was.

phrases.english: Once the Boethusians corrupted matters,
phrases.notes: They tried to mislead the בית דין with false witnesses.

phrases.english: they enacted that they would not accept
except from those who are known.
phrases.notes: Known to the בית דין, or vouched for as in step 22.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ מִכׇּל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the historical background for the rule in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the בייתוסים, the חכמים enacted that testimony on the new moon is accepted only from known witnesses.

steps.title: What does "another" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by "another" person and begins to suggest that it means one person. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is meant by "another"? If you say one person,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking what "another" means. It starts testing the simplest reading, that only one person is sent. This is a setup line, and the next passage will finish the thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally testimony requires two witnesses, so it is surprising if only one companion is enough to vouch for someone. By opening with "if it means one," the גמרא is preparing to show a difficulty with that reading. It will then explain what "another" really means.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
What?
One

steps.confusionAlert: The text breaks off in the middle of a sentence after "חד". The question is not finished yet, so do not treat "one" as the answer.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is "another"?
phrases.notes: Asks for the meaning of the word in the משנה.

phrases.english: If it means one,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud. It is heading toward the problem that one witness is usually not enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing the word "אחר" from step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether "another" in the משנה means one person or more than one.
